# s12 — Render TeX math without a browser or network

Pandoc writes TeX math as MathML. WeasyPrint does not render MathML, so a PDF
shows the flattened symbols followed by the TeX source (`Pout=G⋅PinP_{out} = ...`).

**Findings:** G5 · **Size:** L · **Trees:** core, install

**2026-10-15** — Owner decisions 2026-10-15: approved mathjax@4.1.3 (Apache-2.0, plain 'mathjax' package; mathjax-full is deprecated) as an optional npm dependency, installed by a separate --with-math installer flag (not folded into --with-mermaid; no browser needed). Scratch evaluation: TeX->SVG in Node works offline, ~40ms. Use svg {fontCache: 'local', linebreaks: {inline: false}} - default inline linebreaking splits into multiple SVGs and WeasyPrint shows only the first. Use tex formatError that throws and remove 'noundefined' so undefined macros error. Output has role=img and data-latex but no aria-label/title; add the TeX source as accessible text. mhchem needs an extra font package (out of scope).

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** math in HTML beyond what the same SVG provides;
numbered equations and cross-references.

## Why

branded-pdf renders `$...$` and `$$...$$` through LaTeX. Equations are common
in RF and test documentation.
